newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia government welcomes smelter project.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia government welcomes smelter project.

text.p: Australian Industry Minister John Moore said on Thursday he welcomed the decision of four companies, including U.S.-based Ford Motor Co, to invest in a A$700 million magnesium smelter in central Queensland.
Moore said the decision clearly demonstrated the potential for a world-class magnesium industry in Australia, which would tap into demand for lighter, stronger materials.
"This development is expected to lead to major additional investment in a magnesium car parts industry in Australia targeted squarely at exports," Moore said in a statement.
Under the plan, Ford would invest A$35 million in the Australian Magnesium Corp's (AMC) pilot magnesium smelter in Gladstone, Queensland.

In addition, Normandy Mining Ltd would invest A$20 million, government-owned Commonwealth Scientific Industrial Research Corp (CSIRO) would invest A$8 million, and Queensland Metals Corp would invest A$5 million.

"The investments announced today will enable work to start on the pilot smelter, and could make Australia a major player in both the magnesium metal and international car components industries," Moore said.
The pilot demonstration plant and feasibility study programme is expected to lead to construction of a commercial smelter in 1999 with operations scheduled to begin in 2002.
